en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.3. Wholesome States of the Formless Realm (Arūpāvacara-kusala) 2.1.3.1. The Four Formless Jhānas of Sixteen Occasions Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm— by completely transcending perceptions of form,
by the disappearance of perceptions of sensory resistance, by non-attention to perceptions of diversity, and accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite space;
and by the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … one enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is accompanied by equanimity— at that time:
There is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on] … these states are wholesome.
What states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of infinite space,

dwelling in the fourth jhāna accompanied by the perception of the base of infinite consciousness, with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … accompanied by equanimity— at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before].
These states are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of infinite consciousness—
Accompanied by the perception of the base of nothingness, with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna,
accompanied by equanimity; at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before] … these states are wholesome.
What states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm, having completely transcended the base of nothingness,

accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and with the abandoning of pleasure … [as before] … entering and dwelling in the fourth jhāna— these states are wholesome.
He dwells accompanied by equanimity; at that time there is contact … [and so on] … there is non-distraction … [and so on] … these states are wholesome.
These are the four formless jhānas, each consisting of sixteen moments.
Wholesome consciousness pertaining to the formless realm.
